newsitem.title: UK: Polish ad industry tripled in three years - report.
newsitem.headline: Polish ad industry tripled in three years - report.

text.p: The fall of communism in Poland opened the floodgates to advertising, transforming a country which had had only one, state-controlled advertising agency into one supporting an advertising industry exceeding $500 million, according to a published report.

From 1992 to 1995 advertising expenditure in Poland doubled each year as large, multinational companies sought to establish their trademarks and raise brand consciousness, the Financial Times reported.

Advertising expenditure in 1995 totalled $561 million, up from $248 million in 1993 and $123 million in 1992. Poland, with a population of 39 million, now supports about 20 large ad agencies and 30 smaller ones, the newspaper said.
But a lack of widespread phone penetration -- only 38 percent of households have telephones -- makes it difficult to track the effectiveness of television advertising, the newspaper said.
Television accounts for 58 percent of all advertising expenditure in Poland and is becoming an increasingly competitive market as the number of privatised channels grows.

The two state-owned channels claim about 60 percent of the viewing audience, but are losing viewers to the Polstat locally-owned station, which has a 20 percent market share. Another commercial station, TVN, which is a joint venture of U.S.-based Central European Media Enterprises and local media company ITI, is soon to enter the market, the newspaper reported.
